m.h:
The profit rate assumes 1,100 kills per hour. Actual profits may be higher or lower depending on speed and luck. With best-in-slot gear, you can expect upwards of ~1400 kills per hour.

Ravenous ghouls are permanently aggressive when the player has a Blood essence equipped. Ravenous ghouls will drop a lot of sharks and monkfish, which are useful for emergency food in case of low life points.

Using Soul Split in combination with a demon horn necklace can make it an AFK method maintaining both lifepoints and prayer. To maximize profits, bring high alch runes to alch splitbark bodys, splitbark legs, and splitbark helms. Also combine potions into (4) and note them with magic notepaper.

Finding a vacent world can be challenging. Using the Quiet world hopping feature may help in finding an empty world.

Killing red dragons gives decent money in the form of their guaranteed drops, dragon bones and red dragonhide, which sell for 881 and 1265, respectively. This makes each kill worth 2,146 coins.

The only non-Wilderness location to kill red dragons is in the Brimhaven Dungeon. Access it using either the Karamja lodestone, a Brimhaven tablet, a charter ship to Brimhaven, or an amulet of glory. Entrance to the dungeon costs 875 coins, unless the Hard Karamja Tasks have been completed. Take the long path south and use the shortcut to enter the area. See the map of Brimhaven Dungeon for more information. Alternatively, if Karamja gloves 4 are worn, the shortcut near the dungeon entrance can be used to get to them much faster.

For those willing to take the risk of high level wilderness, Red Dragon Isle potentially offers the advantage of a nearby banker, William, who wanders both inside and outside of the gates. Alternately, those who have the Wilderness sword can use it to teleport to the Wilderness herb patch, which allows for quick returns from regular banks outside the Wilderness.

Red dragons are weak to crossbow bolts, but with high level weapons, any style will work. Super antifire is strongly recommended, as it will allow players to dual-wield weapons instead of having to wield anti-dragon shield or equivalent. Using a Beast of Burden is also helpful to cut down on the number of bank runs. With relatively high combat stats, each kill takes about 10 to 13 seconds on average. It is suggested to use a TokKul-Zo or ring of duelling to quickly bank.

Using a Sign of the porter II (28 Divination) or higher will automatically bank red dragonhides.

If a player doesn't have the level for super antifire potions but does have level 37 Prayer, they can instead use regular Antifire potions combined with Protect from Magic, which will provide complete immunity from chromatic dragonfire.

The chance to receive drops can be increased with the completion of the Wilderness achievements and having a revenant drop enhancer in the inventory while killing revenants. Completion of the wilderness achievements increases the amount of drops by ~5.25% and the revenant drop enhancer increases it by ~11.11%.

Players are recommended to kill ripper demons in the wilderness with a Dwarven siege engine with a magic setup. See Ripper Demon/Strategies for recommended strategies.

Ripper demons are level 96 Slayer monsters that are found underneath the Abbey of St. Elspeth Citharede and the deep wilderness. They use weak, but accurate melee attacks that can hit up to 1,330 damage per hit. Ripper demons can attack up to three times per auto-attack, which essentially triples their damage, although each hit is independently rolled off the player's defensive bonuses.

As the demons attack, they fill up an adrenaline bar. Once filled, the demon will jump into the air (they may either use it immediately, or wait longer), with a shadow appearing west of the player's position. If the player doesn't move away from this shadow, the demon inflicts a 32,000 hard typeless damage hit, essentially killing the player in one hit. This damage is only taken if the player is next to or underneath the shadow; simply moving one space away from the shadow is sufficient enough to avoid damage.

The demons are static upon starting combat. If the player is not next to them when they perform their next attack, they will instead teleport and apply Slaughter.

In addition to these mechanics, when the player falls below 35% health, nearby demons will become aggressive, so make sure health is kept high.

Protect/Deflect Melee should be used with Soul Split flicking, as the demons can pile a lot of damage from their attacks. A vampyrism aspect or scrimshaw also helps in recovering some health.

With Ancient Summoning you can bind ripper demons with Binding contracts. The demon is bound into the contract, allowing players to use Ripper Demons as offensive familiars. They are stronger than steel titans, and fetch a hefty price on the Grand Exchange due to this. Note that magic notepaper must be brought along, as a binding contract is made after each demon is killed, and they will not be made if the player's inventory is full.

If players are intending to make binding contracts, players should instead opt for an attuned ectoplasmator with a demon horn necklace instead, to conserve inventory space, despite losing some profit from the cost of ghostly essence. They may also use infernal urns.

Players may also utilise the Death Note relic power to note the infernal ashes for additional profit.

The profit rate assumes 620 kills per hour, while not on a Slayer task. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Members of the Order of Ascension are killed for their ascension keystone drops. Rorarii are the best targets for large quantities of kills owing to their low life points and high population. With high end gear, upwards of 620 kills can be attained per hour. While on a slayer task, rorarii also have a chance to drop ascension grips worth 1,677,453 gp, for an averaged profit of 815.88180933852 round 0 gp per kill or 505846.72178988 round 0 gp per hour.

Attacking a rorarius prompts the surrounding rorarii to attack you, meaning they cannot be taken down one-by-one. With high level armour, the attacks will not do large amounts of damage, but over time it will add up. Using food or Soul Split, lost life points can be healed easily. Aggression potions can be used to ensure that rorarii automatically attack you.

The best approach with rorarii is to use multi-targeting attacks. Ricochet does damage to two additional targets however the two targets damaged when attacked will not trigger more rorarii to attack so it is advised not to use it depending on your level of attention. Bombardment will damage all enemies adjacent to your target and should be used when 3 or more rorarii are standing together. Corruption Shot is highly effective if unlocked, with it spreading its damage over time effect to nearby rorarii. The same may be done with Incendiary Shot, though this will take a second to fire and will drain all of your adrenaline. Incendiary shot also gives a 30 second buff wherein all critical hits add 10% to your adrenaline; however this benefit may not be very useful considering the lack of ranged abilities.

When no multitargeting is available, focus on one rorarius at a time. Use abilities such as Dazing Shot and Binding Shot followed by Piercing Shot. While bombardment is not available, use Snap-shot and Rapid Fire as your threshold abilities. Remember to be mindful of your health at all times and your prayer points if using Soul Split.

Avoid fighting rorarii near other members of the Order, particularly capsarii who can heal their fellow members. The most optimal locations are the entrance and the room just east of Tertius' laboratory, with both areas containing 9 spawns relatively free of other members apart from a single Scutarius. The former location is significantly better, due to a lack of obstructing objects. If neither of these spots are available or the player is unwilling to use it, the group of rorarii west of the ascended Guthix is an ideal location. See here.

The rorarii's main drop are the ascension keystones, which means that at a kill rate of 600 per hour, you are likely to average about 9 keystones per hour. They also drop maple logs, gold ore, and noted potato with butter, which are not worth picking up as it slows down kills per hour. They also drop alchables like tiny spiky rune salvage, which may or may not be worth picking up.

A blood amulet of fury is an easy way to get your lifepoints restored, and it works on more rorarii at a time.

m.pg: Money making guide/Killing skogres and zogres
m.h:
The profit rate assumes 240 kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Skogres and zogres can be found in Jiggig during and after the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest, and they always drop the ogre coffin keys that are used to loot ogre coffins. Since the bones from the coffins are quite valuable, the keys are valuable and skogres/zogres can be very worthwhile to kill.

The undead ogres are located south of Castle Wars, in the main Jiggig area past the skull barrier. The easiest way to get here (and to bank) is by using the ring of duelling.

They are level 56 and only have 2000 life points, but there's a hitch -- unless you're using the ogre composite bow and brutal arrows, your damage will be reduced to 25% of what it would normally be. Since the ogre bow is a low-level weapon and brutal arrows can be difficult to obtain, it's often better to accept the reduction in damage and fight them with high-level, non-specialised items. Both monsters are weak to fire spells, but this seems to only give a boost in accuracy -- and since the creatures are low-level, you should generally be hitting 100% of the time regardless. Using melee is not recommended as the zogres/skogres have a long death animation and it's worth it to kill one, walk over to it, attack another one from a distance, and pick up the key once it shows up.

You should do this on a populated world, as the location is nearly always empty, and on low-population worlds the six monsters in the main pen may not respawn in time. It should only take 10-20 seconds to kill one even with the damage penalty, so a full inventory might take 8-10 minutes. Banking is very quick at Castle Wars. After you've finished, sell your keys on the Grand Exchange, but keep in mind that as ogre coffin keys have a low buying limit, you may be able to sell them in bulk for a higher price.

Alternatively, you could loot coffins with the keys you've obtained. This is more efficient since it saves banking time and can even be used between monster respawns. See Money making guide/Looting ogre coffins for more information.

The profit rate assumes 150 kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Nihils are highly lucrative to kill, as it drops the summoning ingredient required to make nihil familiars, which are frequently used in high-level combat. 87 summoning is required to make the pouches from the untradeable ingredients.

To reach the location, teleport to the World Gate via the Sixth-age circuit, or teleport to the Eagles' Peak lodestone and walk south. Dial the location to Freneskae and choose "The Pit". Walk to the centre of the pit and choose spawn nihil for slayer/combat. Remember to equip the Shard of Zaros, otherwise all nihils will be aggressive upon spawning.

Smoke nihils are the easiest to kill among the 4 nihils, due to their stat draining properties being easily negated by overloads, and being relatively weak to ranged. Find a corner with high spawn rate of smoke nihils, and place corruption shot at the front of the ability bar. Bait several smoke nihils together, and walk them with fragmentation shot to increase damage taken as they move towards you. The high density of nihils means that corruption shot can take out almost half the hp of other nihils while you pick out the smoke nihils. Kill other low hp nihils when you come across them.

Since the most valuable drop is the summoning ingredient (aviansie talons in the case of smoke nihils), prioritise picking those up and filling your beast of burden with them. Collect the elder charms as well to make the pouches. With 81 divination, you can use 10 elder energy to convert the aviansie talons to the most profitable summoning ingredient, which is usually Icyene feathers due to the popularity of the ice nihil (familiar), however it's wise to check the sale price to make sure. Blood nihil pouches can sometimes be more profitable as well. Make the pouches with 150 elder energy each, and sell on GE.

100 kills is based on the assumption of (1) t90 ranged weapons and t70 power armour augmented with standard perks, (2) using anguish, soul split, corruption shot and walking with fragmentation shot, (3) using overloads, (4) only picking up the aviansie talons, with charming imp picking up the elder charms.

m.h:
There are three snakes right next to the bank deposit chest north of Trouble Brewing on Mos Le'Harmless. These snakes always drop snake hide which is worth 5962 coins each. After obtaining an inventory full of snake hides, the hides may be deposited via the bank box. Each snake only has 250 life points, so they may be killed easily in one hit with a strong weapon. High level players will be able to kill upwards of 300 snakes per hour (1 snake every 10-12 seconds makes a full inventory every 5.5 minutes or so, resulting in around 313 snakes per hour minus the bank time).

Low level players should beware of aggressive jungle horrors which may be found near the western snake. You can minimise the time spent in their attack range by cycling your snake-killing from east-to-west (east snake, centre snake, west snake, repeat). However, this mainly applies to mages, as they will still be standing in the jungle horrors' range when killing the centre snake if cycling from west-to-east (although the horrors can still chase and hit melee players). If the jungle horrors inflict more damage than a player can handle, it is recommended to not kill the western snake in order to completely avoid the jungle horrors. If necessary, food and/or healing abilities should be used to maximise the number of kills per hour. If only killing two of the snakes, the number killed per hour will be significantly less, and therefore profit will be greatly reduced.

Optional: (Note: depending on your graphic settings, this tip may not apply to you)

The snakes, with their small, thin, yellow/brown, low-to-the-ground bodies, can often be hard to see among the tall grasses and green/brown ground of Mos Le'Harmless (especially the eastern-most snake, which spawns in a patch of tall grass). To make the snakes easier to see, you can customise your graphics settings to make the ground less detailed. Go to "Graphics settings", then "Custom". In this menu, toggle "Ground decorations" and "Textures" to "Off" (toggling "Textures" automatically toggles "Scenery Shadows" off as well). This makes it significantly easier to quickly spot the snakes by removing a lot of the grass, shadows, and other details that can obscure the ground. To spot the snakes even more quickly, you may wish to check the minimap for the yellow dot. Memorising the spot where each snake spawns helps significantly; if you can kill them fast enough, you can run up on each snake as it spawns, giving them no time to slither away.

Six level 18 spellwisps are found north-west of Wizard's Tower. While they are weak to Ranged, other combat skills could also kill them with ease due to their low health. They drop various items such as impious ashes (which is a 100% drop), water talismans, and a variety of runes.

In order to obtain a rate of around 500 kills per hour, it's recommended to kill the wisps quickly in a clock-wise or counter clock-wise fashion. When you finish killing one wave, you have around 30 seconds to loot the items with Area loot and prepare for the next wave by the next spawn location. Once your inventory is almost full (less than 10 spaces left) you should kill one wave and then, instead of looting the items, deposit your current items by right clicking and choosing 'Deposit Items' on Wizard Myrtle who is stood on the west side of the entrance to the Wizard Tower near the arches. It is possible to accomplish even more than 500 kills per hour by using strategies such as World hopping.

For lower levelled players, you can use the Legacy Combat Mode in order to kill the spellwisps faster, possibly even one-hitting them. This, however, prevents you from using useful movement abilities such as Surge.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 750 kills per hour and use of the gear setup below. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed. Over 1000 kills per hour is possible with fully optimised gear and an Inquisitor staff, at the expense of AFK time.

Setup

The main priority of this setup is boosting damage and accuracy against the warriors to maximise drops. To this end, the Undead Slayer perk, Salve amulet (e), and 3 pieces of ghost hunter equipment provide a total 37% bonus damage against the warriors, drastically increasing kills per hour (with the ghost hunter equipment also providing an extra 10% experience per hour).

Secondly, this setup is designed to allow for high kills per hours with minimum game interaction. Potion reservoirs are used to allow players to stay AFK for up to five minutes at a time, only checking back in to note potions. Players who don't mind checking in more often can use weapon poison+++ and Torment along with super prayer renewal potions and an ancient elven ritual shard to upkeep prayer.

Lastly, a large rune pouch packed with air, fire, and nature runes is used to save inventory space and allow for alching occasional rare drop table drops.

Maxed Gear= This setup incorporates many of the suggested items to maximise efficiency for minimum effort. An enhanced gold accumulator is assumed to be on the toolbelt, and the Luck of the Dwarves relic power is assumed to be activated, freeing up the ring slot for a ring of vigour. The combination of Enhanced Excalibur, Sacrifice, and a blood necklace take care of sustain. With this setup, players only need to check in once every five minutes. A legendary pet is recommended to pick up potion drops.

Steel dragons are level 100 metal dragons. Like other dragons, steel dragons are capable of using long-ranged dragonfire, so protection is essential. They are weak to water spells, but can just as easily be killed with melee or range with the appropriate levels and equipment. Steel dragons can be found in Brimhaven Dungeon (and its resource dungeon), at Ghorrock and in Kuradal's Dungeon (while on a slayer task).

Killing steel dragons can be profitable due to their drops of dragon bones and various rune salvage. To increase the duration between bank trips, a spring cleaner can be used to alch/dissmantle salvage. An upgraded bonecrusher has the ability to automatically pick up bones to further increase killing time vs looting.

This boss fight consists of only phase 2 of the fight done during Hero's Welcome against the abomination. The boss's health will immediately be reduced to 66,000 as the fight begins. The Ragged Abomination possesses five attacks:

  1. A basic melee attack that has a high accuracy that scales to a player's equipment
  2. A charge attack used when the player moves too far away from the Abomination that stuns the player and then performs two melee attacks
  3. A fireball that can be released with its melee attack that follows the player and deals 5% of their maximum health in damage upon impact. The surrounding squares will be set alight and burn the player for 3.33% of their maximum health per tick; dragonfire protection has no effect whatsoever on this attack
  4. A slam attack that stuns the player and deals damage equal to 1/8 of their maximum health; an onscreen warning message will show
  5. Rocks falling from the ceiling that deal 3.33% of the player's maximum health in damage. The falling rocks can land anywhere, including any safespots the player may use.

As its attacks are scaled to player's equipment, power armour should be used instead of tank armour as they would provide the same defensive properties; Protect from Melee or Deflect Melee will still halve the damage output, however. Experienced players will find that Soul Split can be used to leech back health they may have lost during the fight. The falling rocks and fire mechanics can be used to the player's advantage as the Ragged Abomination can also take damage from these attacks while in the area of effect, dealing even more damage to its already low health; these cannot deal the final blow to the boss.

Unless using Animate Dead with magic tank armour, the fight involves moving around in order to avoid the AoE damage from fire and falling rock as well as the slam, so players may find it easier to manage if they use Ranged or Magic. Melee can be a viable option if a player uses a halberd-style weapon, and/or has the ability to use Bladed Dive.

This guide assumes that the player gets 35 kills a hour, or about a kill every 2 minutes. However, due to its low health, players with tier 90 equipment will find that they can get kills in 30 seconds to 1 minute, effectively doubling the profit shown.

m.t: Killing the Arch-Glacor (Normal Mode, AFK with 1 mechanic)
m.h:
The profit rate assumes 50 kills per hour with 1 mechanic active, with the enriched pontifex shadow ring being overcharged and enriched. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed and ring upgrades.

With only the Flurry mechanic active, it is possible to stand directly in front of the Arch-Glacor, without being moved by any of its attacks. This allows for the boss to be passively killed whilst AFK. In order to maximise profit, it is important to wear your Pontifex shadow ring, if it is available and upgraded to receive Elder troves, as they help contribute to overall profit alongside Wen pages.

A passive form of healing is recommended to offset the boss' damage.

  • Conjure Vengeful Ghost provides enough healing to keep your health full.
  • Soul Split while using the Penance aspect will keep your health and prayer full at all times, provided you deal enough damage to keep yourself healed.
  • Protection prayers can be used, but will most likely need to be accompanied by a healing method like Vampyrism, Scrimshaw of vampyrism, or some other method.
  • A Bunyip familiar can help provide passive healing for very cheap.

m.t: Killing the Arch-Glacor (Hard Mode) (Hard Mode 200 killstreak)
m.h:
This guide is meant as a frame of reference for streaking at Arch Glacor, actually completing a 200 killstreak is sufficiently hard that it has its own grandmaster combat achievement, so should not be taken lightly. The profit rate assumes an average of 14 kills per hour across all the entire streak, early kills will be significantly faster and latter kills will be slower. Profit is massively reduced if you die during a kill, as you will lose items, and likely lose all of your uniques.

Uniques

The rate of uniques is given by the calculator, which is 1.0372 cores per streak and 1.6422 of each of scriptures and artefacts. The expected number of nilas drops per streak is 2, but the quantity dropped ranges from 2 to 42, depending on when in the streak it drops, for an average of 44 per streak.

Commons

The quantity of commons at arch glacor also increases with streak length, however the formula for this is less well understood. Data taken by users DontKillMeDK and Alsang who performed 6 complete 200 killstreaks in 2024/25 was used for the values shown here, but there will be a large variance in value obtained if a high value drop such as Medium blunt orikalkum salvage is obtained near the end of a streak, when the quantity is very high.

More information on killing The Arch-Glacor on Hard Mode can be found in the Hard Mode Arch-Glacor Strategy guide.

m.h:

This setup prioritises the lowest resource input available, making it a low-maintenance solution to killing the boss. It avoids using cannonballs, making it a better alternative to the traditional strategies, saving Ironmen resources.

The profit rate assumes 54 kills an hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your kill speed.

To get to the boss's cave, use a games necklace or combat portal at the Max Guild or Boss portal at War's Retreat.

While Necromancy only deals 50% damage due to not using a spear, it's still a very viable style to kill the boss with low effort and good healing abilities.

Recommended ability bar: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9          

  • For the Conjure Undead Army, right-click and customise it to only spawn the Skeleton Warrior, Vengeful Ghost, and the Putrid Zombie

This method will yield around 54 kills an hour without using an Oldak coil. The use of an Oldak coil will increase the kills/hr, while also increasing input cost. This ability bar utilises the Spectral scythe instead of the Oldak coil to deal with the Dark cores that spawn and deal rapid damage. If using an Oldak coil, you can prioritise other, more damaging attacks like Finger of Death.

In order to kill Corporeal Beast with low effort, a balance of health regen, prayer restoration, and kill speed is needed. Health is upkept through Soul split, the Vengeful Ghost's healing, and the Enhanced Excalibur. Prayer is upkept through the Penance aspect, the Elder overload salves, and the Ancient elven ritual shard (if needed). Kill speed is improved with the Deathdealer's set bonus to apply Death Mark, instantly killing the boss when below 20,000 health when applied.

Soul split should be the only prayer/curse used, as any damage-boosting ones will drain prayer too quickly, requiring additional prayer restoration. This setup avoids using Cinderbane gloves, as the additional chance to apply Death Mark is more valuable, and further reduces repair costs.

Options if lower gear/setup isn't working

There is very little chance of dying if all recommended gear is used. However, if you are a lower Necromancy level, or are missing some items, you might run into issues. The following are recommendations to increase survivability:

  • Use Darkness every 12 minutes to dodge 20% of attacks
  • Customise Conjure Undead Army to also conjure the Phantom Guardian, further reducing incoming damage by 5%
  • Use Deathwarden armour instead of Deathdealer (this will lower kills per hour, but will greatly increase survivability)
  • Use Oldak coil to help deal with Dark core spawns (this will increase kills per hour while increasing supply costs)

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 15 kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

The giant mole is the sole drop source of the numbing root, each of which sells for 105,606 gp.

Magic is the most efficient way of dealing with the Giant Mole - magic armour will best resist the Giant Mole's melee attacks, and the Giant Mole has the weakest defence against Magic.

Pursue the Giant Mole throughout her chambers, and use magic throughout the kill. In mini-mole sections, use Chain and Dragon Breath to leave at most 1 mini-mole alive before refocusing on the Giant Mole again. Use enhanced abilities for damage output when possible, unless you need to take out mini-moles first or are waiting on the Giant Mole to Berserk in the northeastern chamber (and thus need to preserve stuns). Wild Magic can be used to cause burst damage before mini-mole summons, or to push excess damage into the mole's next phase. Adrenaline stall as needed when moving between chambers, trapped in mud (Anticipation and Freedom can still be used while trapped), or between kills.

Due to magic free-to-play weapons being at most tier 55, only air runes to cast Air Blast are necessary - stronger Blast spells will provide no further benefits due to magic damage being capped by the weapon's tier.

Similar approaches can also be performed with two-handed melee weapons, though this will have comparatively higher Attack requirements versus Magic to avoid losing hit chance (85 Attack for 100% hit chance using gravite weapons).

Food requirements can vary greatly between fights due to the nature of the mole's final phase - getting certain patterns such as Berserk and Rockfall simultaneously can result in large amounts of unavoidable damage. Consider using Devotion or Debilitate in response to such patterns to limit the damage you'll take.

If food supplies outlast available prayer points to maintain Protect from Melee, a prayer potion or twisted bird skull necklace can be brought to sustain trips.

rq.t: Slayer Dungeon with tormented demons placed

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 145 kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Tormented demons drop a variety of unique dragon items: dragon limbs, dragon claws, and components of the dragon platebody. Tormented demons have a unique behaviour in combat because they use and change protection prayers based on the combat style dealing them the most damage at any given time. Unlike with most monsters, protection prayers and deflect curses render their attacks almost completely useless; your prayer will either successfully block the attack or reduce the damage to 1. In spite of this, this guide encourages the use of soul split, as it is intended to be done AFK, so prayer switching is unnecessary and impractical.

Behaviour

There are 3 unique behaviours of tormented demons: their fire shield, their protection prayers, and their roar.

The tormented demon's fire shield greatly reduces the amount of damage it takes from all attacks; however, it is easily removed for 1 minute when the demon takes damage from darklight or holy water. Once removed, attacks will deal full damage. They always spawn with their shield up.

All demons start off protecting from melee attacks; however they can switch between protection from all 3 sides of the combat triangle. When protecting itself from any combat style, all damage is nullified, and thus it may be only damaged with the other 2 styles. When the demon has endured 310 damage from a style (calculations done in legacy mode as that is what you will be using to kill them: x10 for EoC numbers), it will switch its prayer to protect against it. Their prayer does not protect from overkill damage; e.g. if 300 then 200 damage is dealt, the full 500 damage will be dealt. The extra damage will not count towards the next 310. When their fire shield is up, the damage before reduction counts towards the 310 rather than the amount it was reduced to.

At frequent intervals, the demon will roar which has either 1 or 3 effects. The first effect is its special attack: a non-blockable, area-of-effect magic attack. Damage may be avoided by dodging the attack, but it cannot be reduced with deflect from magic. The other effect of the roar is actually 3 at once; it will randomise its attack style, weakness, and stat increase/decrease. As the changes are random, it is possible for a roar to cause no change to the demon's abilities. There is no correlation between weakness and attack style. Demons are reluctant to use the second effect of the roar if their target is not protecting/deflecting against the style they are currently using.

Tormented demons will only attack with ranged or magic from a distance and will also attack with melee when you are in range. Their roar only switches between magic and ranged; melee is always available to them without having to switch. Note that if you use either ranged or magic on a demon that is currently using melee and it cannot reach you, it will cause it to roar and switch to ranged or magic. Familiar damage done to the demon seems to times by three approximately when calculating enough damage for them to switch prayers. For example, if a Smoke Nihil were to hit 120, the demon would switch to protect from magic, as this would equal 360 when multiplied by 3 and exceed the damage limit of 310.

Fighting

Tormented Demons can be essentially AFK'd in a personal slayer dungeon if you are using an enhanced darklight, and off-hand ranged weapon, have a smoke nihil familiar summoned, and are using legacy combat. This is by far the easiest method to kill tormented demons, and allows them to be utilised as a fairly effective, low-effort, money-maker. This strategy provides access to all three combat styles (Melee from the darklight --which provides the most damage-- ranged from your off-hand weapon, and magic from the smoke nihil). This is important because it forces the demon to use protect from magic and protect from ranged more frequently than it uses protect from melee. This will allow your darklight to hit upwards of 600 (legacy mode), which allows for the demon to be slain in only a few hits and with minimal inputs. Paired with soul split and various combat-aiding auras, this strategy can be done almost entirely AFK, looking at the screen only to renew potions and pick up drops.

Strategy

Have one tormented demon soul in a large room of your, or a friend's, personal slayer dungeon. Use a mainhand enhanced darklight, off-hand ranged weapon (Off-hand shadow glaive or better is suggested for the high accuracy), and a smoke nihil familiar. Turn on legacy combat, auto-retaliate, a combat aura, and soul split/melee boosting prayer. Using a Demon horn necklace paired with an Attuned ectoplasmator and super prayer renewal potions allows for nearly 100% prayer sustainability, removing the need for (many, if any) sips of prayer potion. With the right auras, one only needs to occasionally activate their Excalibur to sustain their health.

Drops

It is possible to get upwards of 165 kills per hour, but the drop rates are calculated for 145 kills per hour. Some of the drop rates are estimated, as the exact drop rates are not known. Actual profit may vary depending on the accuracy of the estimations for base drops, but the majority of the profit comes from items which have a known drop rate.

If the tortoises are being killed at the Tree Gnome Stronghold, one of the three tortoises are mounted and will, upon being killed, leave three gnomes (gnome archer, gnome mage, and gnome driver) that start attacking you. When killed, these will only drop bones.

Unicows may be killed for their 100% drop rate of unicorn horns, which are commonly used for both Herblore and Summoning. These creatures may be created in the Tower of Life by placing a unicorn horn and cowhide on the north-western altar. Unicows have a combat level of level 82 and attack using magic. Lower levelled players may wish to equip ranged armour, but food should not be necessary.

With an Ardougne cloak, the unicows have a chance of dropping noted unicorn horns instead, saving inventory space. Due to an update, this noted effect is permanently enabled and there is no way to disable it in order to guaranteed un-noted drops. However noted unicorn horn can be un-noted one at a time by either a right-click option on the Altar, or 'use' the horn on the Altar. With one unicorn horn and a war tortoise and inventory full of cowhides, it is possible to create and kill up to 45 unicows per trip. This will usually generate about 90 unicorn horns. Banking may be done via the fairy ring (code ). Returning to the Tower of Life may be done via the fairy ring once more or using the Ardougne cloak teleport to the Kandarin Monastery. Six or more trips per hour are feasible.
